Calculate a binary timescape metric for each raster cell

Source: R/raster.R
ts_raster_metric.Rd

Applies one named timescape metric independently to every cell of a terra::SpatRaster, treating its layers as ordered time steps. Raster cells must contain only 0, 1, or NA through time. A cell containing any NA receives an NA result.

Usage

ts_raster_metric(r, metric, ...)

Arguments

r

A terra::SpatRaster whose layers are ordered time steps.

metric

One exact metric name returned by ts_list_metrics().

...

Named metric-specific arguments passed to ts_metric(), including include_boundary_gaps = TRUE for gap metrics and a positive whole number min_core_period for core metrics. Omitting min_core_period uses 15 time steps and warns once per raster call, rather than once per cell.

Value

A one-layer terra::SpatRaster containing the selected metric.

Examples

r <- terra::rast(nrows = 2, ncols = 2, nlyrs = 4)
terra::values(r) <- matrix(
  c(
    1, 1, 0, 1,
    0, 0, 0, 0,
    1, 0, 1, 0,
    1, 1, 1, 1
  ),
  nrow = terra::ncell(r),
  byrow = TRUE
)
ts_raster_metric(r, "n_periods")
#> class       : SpatRaster
#> size        : 2, 2, 1  (nrow, ncol, nlyr)
#> resolution  : 180, 90  (x, y)
#> extent      : -180, 180, -90, 90  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
#> coord. ref. : lon/lat WGS 84 (CRS84) (OGC:CRS84)
#> source(s)   : memory
#> name        : n_periods
#> min value   :         0
#> max value   :         2
